Thanks again for the time today - great to see the FinData pipeline and the use cases you described for structured risk summaries and anomaly explanations. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Recommendation for initial eval models: redwood-qa-3b (fast, cost-effective baseline) and llama-2-13b-chat (higher-quality, larger-context variant).
- Suggested config: INT8 quantization for the 13b where acceptable, batching target 4-8 requests, and KV caching enabled for repeated prefixes.
- Focused evals: (1) JSON schema compliance for your risk_summary schema, (2) function-calling tests for our tool that returns structured alerts, (3) quality/regression checks vs your golden prompt set.

I attached a first-pass prompt set and our benchmark summary (pdf). Please review the CSV and let us know which 10-20 golden examples you want prioritized.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm prioritized prompt examples by EOD Thursday.
2) We run a 48-72 hour eval across both models with schema validation and provide a results dashboard + regression notes.
3) Schedule a 30-min checkpoint after the initial run to align on pass/fail criteria.

If you have bandwidth, I can include a short test that exercises retries/backoff to simulate intermittent function timeouts - we've seen that surface structured-output flakiness in a small subset of cases.

- What does your function-calling retry behavior look like on timeouts? Do you support idempotency keys so we don't double-act on an alert?
- Any concerns about hallucinations when the model is asked to produce structured fields like account_id or risk_score?

I'll pull together 15 golden examples and share by Thursday morning. Also looping in our engineering lead (solutions@findata.com) on the checklist.

Best,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: model fit & tool-calling evals - FinData POC next steps

Hi Sarah - thanks for the questions, good ones. Short answers + plan below.

1) JSON schema validation: our eval harness can run in two modes - strict and permissive.
   - Strict: enforces types and required fields exactly; any mismatches are flagged as failures.
   - Permissive: tries lightweight coercion (e.g., "123" -> 123) and reports warnings.
   For production, we usually recommend strict mode for downstream determinism. We'll run both and show diffs.

2) Function-calling & retries: Redwood's runtime supports configurable retries with exponential backoff for transient tool errors. We also support idempotency keys passed with the call so your alerts system can deduplicate. We'll enable idempotency by default for the POC runs.

3) Hallucination mitigations: recommended mitigations are (a) constrained response schemas + required fields, (b) verification step where model-provided ids are cross-referenced against a sample of ground-truth keys, and (c) a conservative threshold on generation temperature (we recommend 0.0-0.2 for structured outputs).

Eval plan:
- We will ingest your 15 examples (thanks in advance) and run the following:
  • redwood-qa-3b (INT8) - baseline for latency/cost
  • llama-2-13b-chat (FP16 where available) - quality-focused variant
  • JSON-schema strict validation pass + permissive pass
  • Function-calling tests with retries (3 attempts, backoff 250ms -> 1s -> 2s) and idempotency on

Deliverables (48-72h after prompt confirmation):
- Benchmark PDF (pass/fail by field, latency percentiles, token cost)
- Failure examples with suggested prompt/operator-level mitigations
- A quick dashboard link (we'll share a temporary view)

Would you like us to include a short synthetic regression test that runs the prior week's production prompts through the new models to check for measurable drift? Many customers find that helps catch subtle regressions early.

Cheers,
Marissa

Attachments: findata_prompt_set.csv, redwood_benchmark_results.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Follow-up: model fit & tool-calling evals - FinData POC next steps

Marissa / Dylan - adding a couple implementation notes from the runtime side that I'll include in the eval config: 

- Model variant: for the 13b run, use the chat-optimized checkpoint with 16k context where possible (helps when prompts include historical transaction slices).
- Quantization: INT8 for redwood-qa-3b is fine. For 13b, we recommend trying FP16 first and fallback to INT8-quant if memory/throughput constraints appear - track accuracy delta.
- Schema checks: we'll run a two-pass validator - parser-level strictness then a post-hoc rule engine (regex+type checks) to reduce false positives from coercion.
- Retries: configure idempotency-key header, max 3 retries, jittered backoff to avoid thundering herd on flaky infra.
- Logging: include token-level traces for 25% of requests to help diagnose where structured fields fail.

I'll post the eval config file to the Drive link (see thread links) and create SUP-2345 in Jira for any follow-up engineering tasks if we see regression signals.

-rishi
